question: Any integer composed of 3ⁿ identical digits divisible by
explanation: A number of 3ⁿ identical digits d equals d·(10^(3ⁿ)−1)/9, which is divisible by 3ⁿ (by induction: 111 = 3·37, and each tripling of length multiplies by a factor whose digit sum is divisible by 3).

question:
The circumference of the two concentric disks are divided into 100 sections each. For the outer disk, 100 of the sections are painted red and 100 of the sections are painted blue. For the inner disk, the sections are painted red and blue in an arbitrary manner. It is possible to align the two disks so that
(A) 100 or more
(B) 125 or more
(C) 150 or more
(D) 175 or more
of the sections on the inner disks have their colours matched with the corresponding section on outer disk.
explanation: The outer disk is effectively 200 sections (100 red, 100 blue). Over all 200 rotations each inner section matches exactly 100 times, so the total is 200 × 100 and the average per rotation is 100. Some rotation therefore gives at least 100 matches (pigeonhole/averaging).

question:
Given a binary tree whose inorder and preorder traversal are given by
Inorder : EICFBGDJHK
Preorder : BCEIFDGHJK
The post order traversal of the above binary tree is

options.A: I E F C G J K H D B
options.B: I E F C J G K H D B
options.C: I E F C G K J H D B
options.D: I E F C G J K D B H

explanation: Root B. Left subtree (EICF, preorder CEIF): C with left E (right child I) and right F. Right subtree (GDJHK, preorder DGHJK): D with left G and right H (children J, K). Postorder: I E F C G J K H D B.

question:
Consider the following statement :
(i) The bandwidth of the A.M., wave depends on the band width of the modulating signal.
(ii) The bandwidth of the A.M., wave depends on the modulation index.
(iii) The bandwidth of the F.M, wave for all practical purpose depends on the amplitude of the carrier.
Of these statements the correct statements are
explanation: AM bandwidth = 2fm, independent of the modulation index, so (i) is true and (ii) false. FM bandwidth (Carson's rule) depends on the frequency deviation, i.e. the modulating-signal amplitude, not the carrier amplitude. (iii) is true only if read that way, so the question is doubtful; (B) is the intended answer.
